method: Playwright Chromium, apps.apple.com Ratings & Reviews page (DOM); oldest 10 of the reviews shown

items.title: Easy to use
items.text: Simple, quick not complicated to add a habit, etc...I like the app for the most part.  A few more features would definitely rank it higher and be something I would highly recommend and use... like creating a daily view, weekly view, monthly view, etc. so you can not have so many habits on one view.  Date display options. When adding a habit have the option to have it be an AM or PM Habit and populate the list by AM, PM, Daily, other, etc With this being said, I search for apps a lot and so far I’ve like this one more than others.

items.title: Good
items.text: I like it for its simplicity, however Screen time will show around seventy notifications slightly more or less for the week and that was with only two habits listed. More than twice the notifications for my meds app. At two a day it should be around 14 a week max. Maybe twice that if I have a habit of not responding on the first notification. However, click on one and they all go away. If someone is paying attention seventy notifications showing up on screen time must be impressive. 🌞

items.title: Simple yet better than most paid apps
items.text: I like that this app allows me to see 5 days worth of progress on all habits on the main screen. Tapping on each habit shows monthly and annual progress, which helps motivate one to keep up with the habit. Overall, I love the simplicity and intuitive nature of the app. In terms of aesthetics, a 7-day streak on the main screen (instead of 5 days) would be ideal. Also, checkmarks are good, but filled in bubbles with sound effects would be better and more rewarding. Likewise, on the monthly/yearly view, filled in bubbles (instead of open circles) would be more aesthetically pleasing.  Other than these minor personal preferences, this app is far better than most habit tracking apps for its simplicity and intuitive interface.

items.title: Awesome but please add ability to have multiple lists
items.text: I’ve downloaded a whole bunch of “habit” and “todo” apps, and this is the only one that comes close to what I want.The only thing is that I want the ability to create multiple habit lists:One for eating habitsOne for exercise habitsOne for other habits So please modify this app to allow that.Otherwise it’s perfect.I was searching for an app that lists all the foods I can eat each day and all the exercises I can do.  Then each day I cross off whatever foods I’ve eaten or exercises I’ve done.  And other habits as well. Then at the end of the week I can see which exercises I’ve done and which foods I’ve eaten.  I like that these habits stay in the same place after I check them off.  Lots of apps don’t do that… they either remove from the list or go to the bottom.  Please make this one change to this app allowing multiple habit lists, and then it will really be perfect!  Also this app is free!  Which is great.A lot of them have monthly subscription.  I would be willing to pay $20 for this app but I don’t like monthly fees.

items.title: Best Free Habit Tracker
items.text: I have tried a few and for me this is the best free habit tracker.  Many free ones limit you to 3-5 habits, but I don’t think there is a limit on this one (I have 16).  I love that I can select the color as I have categories of habits (health, mind, cleaning, work).  I’ve also added the widget so I can check the boxes for the day without having to open the full app.  It’s very satisfying to check the boxes and watch my habit “rings” fill in as I do them more consistently.  I can also see the ones that I most commonly miss.  For those, I have used the feature to add a reminder at a certain time. Overall, I really enjoy this app and use it daily.

items.title: Exactly what it claims to be
items.text: It’s a simple little habit tracker that shows a few days of progress at a time and sends you reminders when you ask for them. Very intuitive design, quite easy to use. And it’s totally free, no paywalls.I am a little confused by the repetitive reminder notifications, and I noticed that if you change time zones the app seems to forget the past few days?? But it’s not enough of a distraction to actually bother me, so yeah.

items.title: 5 backwards days? What is the point?
items.text: I just started using the app and the use of 5 days in the wrong order is really off-putting. It would be infinitely better to have all 7 days and in order so I can see the week’s progress. I do not understand the 5-day week that shifts depending on what day it is. Make it start on Sunday or Monday and not move days. Also, a check mark instead of an X would feel more like you completed it, and like someone else said, a short phone vibration when you tap to check it off would feel more official and rewarding. Just some suggestions but very much recommended for better user interaction.

items.title: It’s really simple
items.text: I mean this is exactly as it says. A simple habit tracker but it doesn’t have extra features of things you might want like maybe for water goals of dinking x amount or reading habits of x number of mins. I’m not disappointed by it and think this is great for people that just need a regular to do checklist. From what I can tell there are no limitations on the app for the number of habits you want to track so you can definitely double up on them but I don’t really like that set up for me personally. It also doesn’t have a multi alarm set up so like I said the simplest tracker for those that have a regular daily one off list.

items.title: Lost in the shuffle
items.text: I loved this app for its clean presentation, simple purpose and great customization. I just wanted a quick checklist for the areas I am working on, and after trying many options, this is the one I chose and loved. I have used it for years. Last week, when I went to record my progress for the night, it opened as if it was a brand new app I had just downloaded; no saved data, no login, just three different payment options. What a terrible way to roll out a new monetized model! Some things are worth paying for, and this is one that I would have. It simply would have taken a notice and some consideration or respect for your loyal users to let them know the model was changing. Instead, it was likely me being locked out of a familiar space and all my data was wiped. There’s no notice, explanation, or alternative. So inconsiderate and scummy.

items.title: Paid user, data lost, subscription push
items.text: I recently paid for this app, though I have used it for many years and may have paid for it before with my old phone. I liked its simplicity over the “services” offered by other apps. From the last update, my habit data is gone. It forced me through an onboarding survey and then prompted me for a subscription. The “Restore Purchases” button doesn’t help. The developer’s website and support links go to a long neglected “Twitter” account, and I’m not on X, anyway, to contact them for any hope of restoring my lost data. I haven’t yet labored to re-enter all of my lost habits, so I don’t know whether the functionality I paid for will still work—if it doesn’t, I will notify Apple of fraud. I have strongly recommended Habitty to friends in the past—I cannot do so after this update.UPDATE: I cannot add more than one habit. It prompts for payment. “Restore Purchases” reports “no purchases found. I will contact Apple.
